{{Short description|Dimensionless parameter in fluid mechanics}}
The '''Hartmann number''' ('''Ha''') is the ratio of electromagnetic force to the viscous force, first introduced by Julius Hartmann (1881{{spaced ndash}}1951) of Denmark.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Moreau|first1=René|title=Magnetohydrodynamics: Historical Evolution and Trends|last2=Molokov|first2=Sergei S.|publisher=Springer|year=2007|isbn=978-1-4020-4833-3|editor-last=Molokov|editor-first=Sergei S.|series=Fluid Mechanics and Its Applications|volume=80|pages=155–156|chapter=Julius Hartmann and His Followers: A Review on the Properties of the Hartmann Layer|doi=10.1007/978-1-4020-4833-3_9|author-link=René Moreau|editor-last2=Moreau|editor-first2=René|editor-last3=Moffatt|editor-first3=H. Keith|editor-link3=Keith Moffatt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hunt|first1=J.C.R.|last2=Shercliff|first2=J.A.|date=January 1971|title=Magnetohydrodynamics at High Hartmann Number|journal=[[Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics]]|volume=3|pages=37–62|bibcode=1971AnRFM...3...37H|doi=10.1146/annurev.fl.03.010171.000345|doi-access=}}</ref> It is frequently encountered in fluid flows through magnetic fields.<ref>{{cite book|author=Cramer|first=Kenneth R.|title=Magnetofluid Dynamics for Engineers and Applied Physicists|last2=Pai|first2=Shih-i|publisher=Scripta Publishing Company|year=1973|isbn=0-07-013425-1|lccn=73009936}}</ref> It is defined by:

: <math>\mathrm{Ha} = B L\sqrt{\frac{\sigma} {\mu}}</math>
where
* ''B'' is the [[magnetic field]] intensity 
* ''L'' is the characteristic length scale
* ''&sigma;'' is the [[electrical conductivity]]
* ''&mu;'' is the [[dynamic viscosity]]
